The mirror ratio and compliance are fine, so the fault is in the output-side gain path, which sets Rout. M1/M2 have matched W/L (5.29 vs 5.32), so the mirror ratio is intact and the 0.3% error is consistent with that. Rout of this cascode is roughly gm4·ro4·ro2, and M4 is the cascode device whose gm·ro product dominates it. M4's W/L (6.635/0.153 ≈ 43) looks reduced relative to the reference cascode M3 (≈287), so M4 is the most likely corrupted element. M2 is next, since its ro contributes directly to Rout and an L or W change there would also show up. M3 is third, because it sets the cascode bias at node b and only affects Rout indirectly.

{"ranking": ["M4", "M2", "M3"], "fault": "M4 (cascode output device) has a wrong size, most likely a reduced W or a shortened/altered L versus design, which lowers its gm*ro gain and drops rout from about 7 MOhm to 6.03 MOhm. Restore M4 to its designed W/L so rout meets the 7 MOhm spec."}
